Non-Surgical Breast Enlargement

Feeling Unhappy About Your Breast Size: Understanding the Feeling and Choosing Next Steps

Many people feel dissatisfied with their breasts at some point. That is common and nothing to be ashamed of.

Home/Non-Surgical Breast Enlargement/Breast Enlargement Without Surgery/Feeling Unhappy About Your Breast Size: Understanding the Feeling and Choosing Next Steps

Many people feel dissatisfied with their breasts at some point. That is common and nothing to be ashamed of. How you respond matters. This page is part of our guide to breast enlargement without surgery.

Where the feeling comes from

Media, social comparisons, comments from others, life changes such as pregnancy or weight loss, and personal history can all play a part. Filters and edited images create unrealistic standards. It can help to notice when the feeling is strongest and what is happening around you at the time.

Pause before acting

A few questions can help:

  • What exactly bothers me, and in which situations?
  • Would I feel the same if no one else saw my body?
  • Am I considering a change for myself or for someone else?
  • Have I had this feeling for a long time or is it recent?

Low-risk steps to try first

  • Professional bra fitting
  • Clothing that suits your body
  • Talking to someone you trust
  • Limiting exposure to social media that makes you feel worse

When to talk to a professional

If you feel intense distress, preoccupation with your appearance, avoid social situations or spend a lot of time checking or hiding your body, speak to a doctor or mental health professional. These may be signs of a condition such as body dysmorphic disorder, which is treatable and which surgery generally does not relieve.

If you are considering a procedure

See a qualified, registered clinician, ask about alternatives including doing nothing, and take time. There is no deadline that justifies a rushed decision. Read our breast enlargement safety guidance before consenting to anything.

Give yourself room to decide

There is no deadline for a cosmetic decision. It can help to wait through a major life change, try low-risk appearance options and write down what you hope would be different afterwards. A good clinician will discuss the option of no treatment without treating it as a failure.

Key takeaway

Your feelings are valid. Decisions about your body are best made calmly, with accurate information and support.
